title: fix(service-storage)!: a stored file's uploader is the user who created it, as an attachment's and a comment's author are
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: updated here — `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` now states that a `sys_file` created through the data API records the signed-in user as `owner_id`, and that such a create with no signed-in user is refused. No published skill teaches writing `sys_file.owner_id` (`git grep` over `skills/` finds none).

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:非系统上下文创建 `sys_file` 时,`owner_id` 一律记为当前会话用户(覆盖请求里带的值),与附件 `uploaded_by`、评论 `author_id` 同一规则;会话没有登录用户的创建被拒绝(403 `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`)。
- **为什么改**:一个文件的上传者就是创建它的人;出处只在创建时记录一次,之后只读(更新侧已是只读)。
- **风险与回滚**:收窄(BREAKING)。经数据接口创建 `sys_file` 时请求里的 `owner_id` 不再生效;上传接口、系统上下文写入、无会话的裸内核调用都不变;控制台不经数据接口创建 `sys_file`,无需改动。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/services/service-storage/src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts`(`recordUploader` 与钩子里 `if (ctx?.session)` 那一行)、`packages/qa/dogfood/test/attachments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts`(数据接口上的新钉)、`.changeset/sys-file-uploader-is-its-creator.md`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.test.ts src/sys-file-storage-owned-columns.integration.test.ts`,预期 `Test Files 2 passed (2)`、`Tests 38 passed (38)`。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

A stored file's uploader is the user who created it, as an attachment's and a comment's author are.

- **Create.** A non-system create of `sys_file` records the session's user as `owner_id`, over whatever the request carries: the stamp the attachment create hook (`sys_attachment.uploaded_by`) and the comment create hook (`sys_comment.author_id`) already apply. It lives in the existing `sys_file` create guard (`installSysFileStorageOwnedColumnsGuard`), beside the storage-owned column strip, so `sys_file` keeps one `beforeInsert` registration.
- **Refused.** A non-system create whose session names no signed-in user is refused with 403 `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, the code and status the attachment and comment hooks answer their own no-user creates with.
- **Unchanged.** The system context keeps the `owner_id` it supplies: the upload doors (presigned, chunked, complete) record the session's user themselves under it, as do imports and migrations. A call with no session at all (a bare kernel) keeps its value too, which is the attachment hook's carve-out. Updates are unchanged: `owner_id` is already read-only after creation, so an update drops a non-system caller's value and reports it in `droppedFields`.
- **One difference from the attachment hook, by design.** The attachment hook passes a context-less call entirely. Here the carve-out covers the uploader only: the storage-owned and file-reference columns are still dropped from a context-less create, because that strip judges every write that is not `isSystem` (as the update strip does) and this rule does not loosen it.
- **Silent, as the attachment and comment stamps are.** The engine reports `droppedFields` / `onFieldsDropped` only for strips it runs itself, it runs none on a `sys_` object's create, and the hook contract has no member for a hook to report one; so the overwrite is not reported, exactly as `uploaded_by` and `author_id` are not.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`, and the `owner_id` comment in `objects/system-file.object.ts`.

## Tests

- **Unit, at the guard** (new `sys-file-storage-owned-columns.test.ts`, 8 cases): the session's user is recorded over another user's id and when none is named; three no-user sessions (a service principal, an organization only, an empty user id) are refused 403 `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` with nothing logged; a system create keeps its value; a bare-kernel call keeps its value and still loses the storage-owned columns; the stamp sits beside the strip.
- **Integration, real engine over sqlite** (`sys-file-storage-owned-columns.integration.test.ts`, 6 new cases): single and batch creates record the caller; a no-user create is refused and writes no row; the upload doors (presign, complete) still record the uploading user; a system create and a system update keep the uploader they write; an update leaves the uploader the create recorded.
- **Dogfood, at the data door** (`attachments-permission-matrix.dogfood.test.ts`, uploader block): an administrator's `POST /data/sys_file` naming another user answers 201 and records the administrator; control, a system create keeps the uploader it supplies. The block's existing pins stay the update-side and upload-door controls: an administrator's PATCH of `owner_id` answers 200 with `owner_id` in `droppedFields`, and (e) the upload door stamps the uploading member.
- **Ablation, one shot** (fix committed first; mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which restored on exit): the stamp line replaced by a no-op, `service-storage` rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight` proved the line absent from `dist/`. Red as predicted: 5 of 38 in the two guard files (the three unit and two integration cases that read the stamp) and the new dogfood pin; every control stayed green. Restore leg: blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, preflight proved the mutation absent and the line present in `dist/`, both runs green again.

## Acceptance notes

- `sys_file.owner_id` has no update-time ownership-transfer path: since the rule that made a row's uploader read-only after creation, the update strip drops a non-system caller's `owner_id`, the holder of the ownership-transfer grant included (measured on `origin/main` 917f024d95: PATCH 200, `droppedFields` names `owner_id`, stored value unchanged). This PR keeps that; only the system context records a different uploader.
- No UI or service creates `sys_file` through the data API (`git grep` over `ui/` and `packages/` finds the one writer, `StorageMetadataStore.createFile`, under the system context), so no caller changes.
